heading: Peckham ‘Top Urban District’
bodyHtml:
Peckham’s reputation has changed considerably in recent years. It’s gone from being one of the most deprived districts in London to one of its trendiest – and property prices are reflecting the shift.

That’s according to research published by Homes and Property, which has found that house price growth in Peckham has outpaced every other UK district since 1995 when records began. Knight Frank carried out the detailed analysis of Land Registry data, which showed prices here have grown by a staggering 1,082 per cent since 1995.

One of the reasons why Peckham has become such a popular hotspot is because many of its unusual buildings have been saved from demolition.

Eileen Conn is named as a key figure in this. She founded the group Peckham Vision, which rescued buildings and spaces in the area around Peckham Rye station. These all “contribute to Peckham’s special identity”, the news provider noted.

“Since 2005, the group have campaigned to highlight reuse and restoration. Existing buildings are a record of social and visual history – they affect the sense of place and identity of an area,” Ms Conn stated.

This goes to show the importance of restoring existing buildings, rather than just demolishing them to make way for new properties. Restoring buildings with care and love can have stunning results, as demonstrated in Peckham.

If you’ve been considering buying a period home, but haven’t taken the plunge yet, now could be the time to do it. Another article for Homes and Property noted that only new build homes have seen prices increase in every borough in the capital since 2014.

Since the referendum to leave the EU, prices of existing homes in the capital have declined by 2.1 per cent, whereas the cost of buying a new-build home has risen by 1.6 per cent in the same period.
